'''Towarzystwo Sportowe Wisła Kraków [[Spółka Akcyjna]]''', commonly referred to as '''Wisła Kraków''' ({{IPA|pol|ˈviswa ˈkrakuf}}), is a Polish professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Kraków]]. They compete in the [[Ekstraklasa]] following promotion from the [[2025–26 I liga]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=4 lata i wystarczy. Wisła Kraków świętuje awans do Ekstraklasy |url=https://polskieradio24.pl/artykul/3684442,4-lata-i-wystarczy-wisla-krakow-swietuje-awans-do-ekstraklasy |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Polskie Radio 24 |language=pl}}</ref> It ranks fourth in the number of [[List of Polish football champions|national titles]] won (13), behind [[Górnik Zabrze]], [[Ruch Chorzów]] (both on 14), and [[Legia Warsaw]] (15), and second in all-time victories. Wisła was founded in 1906 under the name TS Wisła ([[Polish language|Polish]]: Towarzystwo Sportowe Wisła). The team plays its home matches at the [[Henryk Reyman Municipal Stadium|Synerise Arena Kraków]].

The club's coat of arms is a red crest crossed by a blue ribbon, with a white star centered on top.

Wisła Kraków was one of the most successful Polish football clubs of 2000s, winning eight league championships since 1999. Along with league titles, Wisła also won the [[Polish Cup]] on five occasions, including the first-ever edition in 1926, and are the [[2023–24 Polish Cup|current cup]] holders. Wisła also enjoyed some success in European competitions in the 1970s, reaching the quarter-finals in the [[1978–79 European Cup]]."}}
